page.title: tinyactors: like SQLite, but for actors
page.description: tinyactors runs statecharts as actors inside your process, millions with most of them asleep, and tests them over thousands of simulated runs.

hero.headline: Like SQLite, but for actors.
hero.lede: tinyactors is a library that runs actors inside your program, each a statechart: about 530 bytes awake and 120 asleep.

section.heading: Write each actor's behavior as one chart.
section.p: A statechart is a state machine whose states nest inside states and run side by side in parallel regions. The W3C wrote it down as SCXML, so a chart means the same in every runtime.
This chart charges a card, waits 30 seconds for an answer, and retries until it has charged three times.

section.heading: Run millions of actors in your process.

claim.p: It runs your actors on your own event loop, in Node.js, Bun, Python, a browser or C.
That is a started actor in Node.js, measured with a million in one process. The C core allocates only from memory you give it.

claim.statement: A sleeping actor keeps about 120 bytes.
claim.p: Idle actors hibernate to your store and wake on their next event. Each operation costs about the same at four million actors as at two.
claim.source: Twice the actors, the same cost

section.heading: Hand a chart to a coding agent.
section.p: A chart holds all of an actor's behavior, so an agent changes it as it would change one function.

item.text: An agent reads the chart, not a call graph spread over a codebase.
A chart sends an event for each effect, and a handler you write performs it, so the agent's change touches no I/O.
Outages, retries and timeouts run on a simulated clock, so the agent checks its change against them at once.

section.heading: Simulate a thousand runs.
section.p: Does the payment ever charge a card four times, or give up too early? A test that waits 30 seconds per retry cannot ask that a thousand times, but a simulation can.

item.text: A handler you write stands in for the payment service. A seeded random number decides whether it answers each charge.
The host runs on a SimulatedClock, which jumps straight to the next timeout.
After each run, the program asserts at most three charges, and no giving up before the third.

section.p: The program runs a thousand seeds and prints whether any run broke a rule:

example.caption: Change attempts < 3 to attempts < 4 and seed 10 fails.

section.heading: Kill your unit tests.
section.p: A unit test checks one run. A property checks every run a generator can make, and a failure shrinks to the smallest run that breaks it.

claim.statement: It passes the W3C's own tests.
claim.p: SCXML defines what every transition does, and tinyactors passes all 191 automatic tests of the W3C suite.
A failing run's trace shows each event the actor took and the states it entered.

section.heading: Build a team chat.
section.p: Five steps, each a program you can run.

item.text: One actor, and a handler for the screens.
Each user is offline, active or away.
One actor decides which rooms exist.
A thousand users, fifty in memory.
Two million actors ran with at most 1000 in memory and the rest in a database.
Running actors move to their chart's next version and keep the state they reached.
A host of two million actors copies into a 165 MB snapshot that another process restores.
Each step an actor takes becomes a span in your OpenTelemetry collector.
